distinguishing_features: Engineered micro-pinhole/reentrant-cavity surface texturing on the cooling vessel wall to create deterministic heterogeneous nucleation sites
Pinning ice nucleation at a specific predicted onset temperature to replace stochastic supercooling bursts
Application to cryopreservation cell-suspension cooling rather than reactor wall fouling suppression
Using existing thermocouple latent-heat-spike data as the pass/fail validation signal
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to make the onset of ice nucleation deterministic and spatially localized at a predictable temperature so that latent heat release and crystal growth do not cause stochastic thermal shock and shear damage to cells during cooling.
parsed.viable_reason: Classical heterogeneous nucleation theory supports that engineered cavities with controlled radius and contact angle lower and pin the required supercooling, and the protocol is testable with standard freezers and thermocouples.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 2 suppresses heterogeneous nucleation via chemistry to avoid wall deposition, whereas the candidate deliberately engineers heterogeneous sites to control and localize nucleation onset, which is a non-obvious inversion of the closest art's approach.
